subject: [PATCH] mm/huge_memory: transfer the pmd dirty bit to the folio on zap

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary: Reviewer David pointed out that the patch should only transfer the pmd dirty bit to the folio on zap for non-anonymous (non-anon) folios, similar to the logic in zap_present_folio_ptes(), and suggested resembling this logic
reviews.raw_body:
We don't need that for anon folios, though. So best to just resemble
zap_present_folio_ptes() logic and do it only for !anon folios?

-- 
Cheers,

David

reviews.author: Kiryl Shutsemau
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Kiryl Shutsemau expressed confusion and skepticism about the discovery of the bug, suggesting that it might be due to the rarity of read-ahead operations on shmem

Gave Reviewed-by

Reviewer Kiryl Shutsemau noted that zap_huge_pmd() drops the rmap under the pmd lock, while TLB flush is deferred to tlb_finish_mmu(), creating a potential silent data loss issue for PMD-order folios. He suggested adding a pmd equivalent of tlb_delay_rmap()/force_flush to handle this case.
reviews.raw_body:
+Hugh.

Oopsie.

I'm confused why it took a decade to discover the bug...
Maybe read ahead of write for shmem is too rare, I donno.

---

Unrelated to your patch, but noticed while looking at it: we drop the rmap
here under the pmd lock, while the TLB flush is deferred to
tlb_finish_mmu(). The pte path handles this with
tlb_delay_rmap()/force_flush (5df397dec7c4), but there's no pmd equivalent:
tlb_flush_rmap_batch() only knows folio_remove_rmap_ptes(), and
zap_huge_pmd() uses tlb_remove_page_size(), which takes no delay_rmap.

Doesn't matter for shmem, but xfs & friends do get PMD-order folios, and
do_set_pmd() makes the pmd dirty+writable once page_mkwrite() has run. So
folio_mkclean() can clean the folio while another CPU still stores through a
stale TLB entry -- silently lost write, no PG_dirty left behind.

I think we need to fix this too.

Wanna give it a try?

reviews.author: Usama Arif
reviews.summary: Reviewer noted that the current implementation of tlb_flush_mmu_tlbonly() and tlb_remove_page_size() can lead to a stale TLB entry being accessed after its rmap entry is removed, resulting in a silently lost write. They suggested adding a new function pmd_zap_needs_tlb_flush() to check if a TLB flush is needed before dropping the rmap entry.

reviews.author: Pedro Falcato
reviews.summary: Reviewer Pedro Falcato questioned the assumption that page_mkwrite is called in the same path as do_set_pmd(), citing write amplification concerns and pointing to a comment in wp_huge_pmd() indicating that COW or write-notify should be handled on the pte level.
reviews.raw_body:
Where do you see page_mkwrite being called in the same path as do_set_pmd()?
Per my understanding of the code, this Should Not Happen, and it really Should
Not Happen for many, many reasons (write amplification being the main one).

Namely, see the comment in wp_huge_pmd():
	/* COW or write-notify handled on pte level: split pmd. */

if file huge pages get mapped writable, that's a bug.
 

-- 
Pedro

reviews.author: Hugh Dickins
reviews.summary:
Reviewer noted that modifying a 2MiB+ hole in a shmem file through an mmap can result in silent data loss due to the pmd dirty bit not being updated, and suggested fixing this by adding a pmd equivalent of tlb_delay_rmap()

Gave Acked-by
reviews.raw_body:
It isn't entirely clear from the report, but this is all about modifying
a 2MiB+ *hole* in a shmem file through an mmap thereof, with first fault
a read fault not a write fault.  I suppose only a few proceed in that way
(though truncating an empty file to some size and then mmap'ing that size
is very normal).

Or everybody who tried to report this bug, wrote their report into a
2MiB hole in a shmem file through an mmap thereof.

Other than holes, all shmem folios are dirty throughout (and re-marked
dirty as soon as brought back from swap): so for most, it doesn't matter
what the pmd says.

This raised a dim memory, took a while to locate what I was remembering:
e1f1b1572e8d ("mm/huge_memory.c: fix data loss when splitting a file pmd")
from 2018.

Not quite the same; but what a pity that one didn't prompt any of us
to look further and find what Usama now has.

2026-08-19.patch_summary: This patch addresses an issue where the pmd dirty bit is not being transferred to the folio when a huge page is zapped, leading to potential silent data loss in certain file systems like xfs. The problem arises because the TLB flush is deferred and can occur after the rmap has been dropped under the pmd lock, causing stale TLB entries to remain. To fix this, the patch aims to transfer the pmd dirty bit to the folio on zap, ensuring that data integrity is maintained even in the presence of concurrent writes.

reviews.author: Lance Yang
reviews.summary:
Reviewer noted that pageout() cannot pass its refcount check due to PMD mapping holding an extra folio reference, which is dropped by mmu_gather only after TLB flush

Reviewer noted that writeback can run folio_mkclean() concurrently with another CPU holding a stale TLB entry reference, causing a silent lost write and missing PG_dirty

Reviewer noted that zap_huge_pmd() only handles one PMD under PTL and suggested flushing the TLB before calling folio_remove_rmap_pmd() to avoid stale TLB entries.
reviews.raw_body:
Right. pageout() cannot pass its refcount check while PMD mapping still
holds an extra folio ref, and mmu_gather drops that ref only after TLB
flush.

---

Yep. Writeback can run folio_mkclean() while that ref is still held,
though, and with rmap already gone it misses the PMD ...

---

zap_huge_pmd() only handles one PMD under PTL anyway ... how about just
flushing before folio_remove_rmap_pmd()?

---8<---
diff --git a/mm/huge_memory.c b/mm/huge_memory.c
index afbb5974bd22..6fb34924ef66 100644
--- a/mm/huge_memory.c
+++ b/mm/huge_memory.c
@@ -2531,6 +2531,14 @@ bool zap_huge_pmd(struct mmu_gather *tlb, struct vm_area_struct *vma,
 	is_present = pmd_present(orig_pmd);
 	folio = normal_or_softleaf_folio_pmd(vma, addr, orig_pmd, is_present);
 	has_deposit = has_deposited_pgtable(vma, orig_pmd, folio);
+	/*
+	 * folio_mkclean() relies on the rmap to find writable mappings.
+	 * Flush stale TLB entries before removing it below.
+	 */
+	if (folio && is_present && !folio_test_anon(folio) &&
+	    pmd_dirty(orig_pmd))
+		tlb_flush_mmu_tlbonly(tlb);
+
 	if (folio)
 		zap_huge_pmd_folio(mm, vma, orig_pmd, folio, is_present);
 	if (has_deposit)
---

Cheers, Lance

reviews.author: Lance Yang
reviews.summary:
Lance Yang noted that in the case of an initial shared write fault on non-DAX XFS, __handle_mm_fault() first tries to create a huge PMD, which fails and sends the fault to handle_pte_fault(). This path leaves an empty PMD without a PTE, calls do_pte_missing(), and eventually leads to finish_fault(), which sees FAULT_FLAG_WRITE and attempts to set a dirty+writable PMD with do_set_pmd(). Lance Yang pointed out that this can lead to silently lost writes if another CPU stores through a stale TLB entry while the folio is being cleaned, and suggested fixing this issue.

The reviewer pointed out that __handle_mm_fault() calls wp_huge_pmd() only when a write/unshare fault hits an existing read-only PMD THP, and that the initial shared write fault above runs page_mkwrite before do_set_pmd() installs the writable file PMD.

2026-08-20.patch_summary: This patch addresses an issue where the pmd dirty bit is not being transferred to the folio when a huge page is zapped, leading to potential silent data loss in certain file systems like xfs. The problem arises because the TLB flush is deferred and can occur after the rmap has been dropped under the pmd lock, causing stale TLB entries to remain. To fix this, the patch aims to transfer the pmd dirty bit to the folio on zap, ensuring that data integrity is maintained even in the presence of concurrent writes.
